why_and_limits: Prime Minister chairs the Central Traffic Safety Measures Council under Articles 14–15 of the Basic Act; the Cabinet Office coordinates its plan preparation and interministerial support. Statutory executive chair, not attendance proof

The council roster names a minister for Financial Services, but NOT a separately named Finance Ministry seat. Public administration finances safety activities through ministry programmes; the 12th Plan does not set one audited, costed central council road-safety budget. Limited financial-services / programme financing interface

National Public Safety Commission chair is an express member; the National Police Agency prepares annual enforcement measures and accident-analysis priorities. Formal public safety representation; operational enforcement by the NPA and prefectural police
Minister of Justice appears in the central council membership; the plan includes traffic-offence investigation, legal assistance and victim remedies. Formal ministry seat; courts not directly members

Fire and Disaster Management Agency, local fire services, medical and rescue bodies are explicitly assigned rescue, first-aid and highway emergency response measures; the Fire Agency is not separately listed as a central council member. Agency-level delivery through internal affairs and local governments

Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry is an appointed member and the plan expressly treats vehicle makers, advanced vehicle technologies, safety standards, inspections and recalls. Formal industry portfolio, not manufacturers holding their own seat

MLIT road-construction and technical organizations are linked through road-works, design, inspection and safety measures; there is no separate construction trade/engineering association seat. Technical engineering portfolio and implementing road authorities, not construction-membership seat

MLIT Minister formally holds a council seat; the plan places safety actions on national road authorities and prefectural road networks, including hazard removal, sidewalks and speed-management infrastructure. Formal roads ministry portfolio with wider delivery network

MLIT Minister has a formal seat and the plan regulates professional drivers, commercial fleets and safe bus/truck services; operators are cooperating implementers, not statutory council members. Formal transport ministerial portfolio

The Internal Affairs and Communications Minister is formally represented and the road plan describes ITS, road warnings and crash-data technologies, but no distinct Digital Minister is on the published member list. Digital/communications technical link, not a dedicated digital-system member

No Environment Minister is included in the published council roster, and no independently accountable environmental road-safety function in the selected council mandate has been verified. The plan mentions emissions co-benefits of ITS but this is not an environmental-sector road safety coordination seat. Environmental benefits are not formal membership

MLIT and local-government councils implement neighbourhood street redesign, universal design, pedestrian and cycling facilities; the central council does not list a separate urban planning or housing minister. Urban/local planning interface rather than a distinct council seat

Health, Labour and Welfare Minister is a published member; health-sector emergency medical services, trauma care and rehabilitation are described in road plan pp. 92–102. Formal ministerial portfolio; service delivery by medical/emergency actors

The Cabinet Office sought public comments, organized a hearing and separately solicited opinions from road-crash victims organizations for the 12th plan. Local traffic-safety associations and residents also participate in implementation. Consultation and partnership documented, not standing nongovernmental central council membership
